land.text: Tripolitania, Cyrenaica and Fezzan, over which the Ottomans 'reestablished direct control' in 1835

predecessors.note: The page: 'In 1835 the Ottomans reestablished direct control over the region'; the month (26 May 1835) is the end of Ali II's reign on the Karamanli page. Cliopatria starts this row in 1840 and keeps a Karamanli shape for 1836-1839.

land.text: Italian Tripolitania and Cyrenaica, which 'later merged into Italian Libya'

successors.note: Italy declared sovereignty by decree on 5 November 1911 and the Treaty of Ouchy was signed on 18 October 1912; Cliopatria's Italian Africa row covers Libya from 1912 (2,946 Libyan cells, the same land as this row's 1911 shape).

capitals.name: Tripoli
capitals.note: Infobox: capital Tripoli. Benghazi was the seat of the Cyrenaican sanjak (independent 1863-1871, under Tripoli 1871-1888, then directly dependent on Istanbul, per the page) and Murzuk of Fezzan.

correction.text: the province of Tripolitania with its sanjaks Tripoli, Khums, Jabal al-Garb, Fezzan and Benghazi (Cyrenaica): 'In 1835 the government of Sultan Mahmud II took advantage of local disturbances to reassert their direct authority'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the years before Cliopatria's row (1840). Cliopatria gives the Libyan coast in 1836-1839 to the Karamanli (166 cells) and to the Ottoman Empire row (87 cells); the page has direct Ottoman control from 1835 and the Karamanli end in 1835. The 1840 shape, cut to Libya, is used for the whole province.

correction.text: the five sanjaks of the province, all in present-day Libya: Tarablus al-Gharb, Khums, Jabal al-Garb, Fezzan and Benghazi

keyframe_review.note: 894,407 km2, 1840-1858, of which 58 cells (roughly 12-15 k km2) lie outside Libya: 47 at 10 N, 44-45 E in Somaliland and 11 on the Tunisian, Niger and Chad edges. The page lists five sanjaks, all in Libya, and names no Somaliland possession; the stray patch is dropped in Cliopatria's own 1885 shape (881,872 km2). The infobox gives no area, so the sanity check is against the 1885 shape only. Libya north of about 22.8 N is the rest.

correction.text: the same Libyan land as 1840, the province reclassified 'from an eyalet to a vilayet after an administrative reform in 1865'

keyframe_review.note: 894,458 km2, 1859-1884, identical to 1840 but for 51 km2: the same Somaliland stray is dropped. Administrative changes the shape does not show: Cyrenaica 'an independent sanjak in 1863 that was directly dependent on Istanbul', 'assigned to Tripoli's supervision in 1871' and 'attached to Istanbul again in 1888'; by 1867 the Tripolitania Vilayet.

881,872 km2, 1885-1894: Libya only (Libya north of about 22.7 N, no Kufra, Ghat only a quarter and Murzuq two thirds inside); the Somaliland patch is gone. The Senussi had their capital at Jaghbub and, in the 1880s, Kufra, which the shape leaves out; the page gives no area and no southern limit.

881,472 km2, 1895-1904: two cells lost on the western edge near Ghadames (29.5-30 N, 9.5-10.6 E) and one gained on the Cyrenaican coast. The Libya-Tunisia page has 'a border on the coast between Tunisia and Tripolitania in 1886' and the line 'then extended southwards down to the vicinity of Ghadames in 1892': the only dated frontier work in these years, and consistent with a three-cell change.

880,043 km2, 1905-1910: six cells lost and five gained along the Saharan edge between about 24 and 30 N; Cliopatria's area falls by 1.4 k km2. The treaty of 19 May 1910 'delimited the border in greater detail' and it was 'demarcated on the ground with pillars in 1910-11', after this shape's span; the Algerian frontier page has no Ottoman-era line. The change is within the precision of the Saharan edge and is left unverified.

880,043 km2 for 1911. Italy declared war on 29 September 1911, bombarded Tripoli on 3 October and captured Tripoli, Tobruk, Derna, Bengasi and Homs between 3 and 21 October; the Ottomans and the Senussi held the interior, so the whole shape stays Ottoman with the coastal towns contested.

correction.text: unchanged for 1912 until the Treaty of Ouchy of 18 October 1912, with the interior still held by Ottoman officers and the Senussi

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row ends in 1911 but the war ended on 18 October 1912, when 'The Ottomans would withdraw all military personnel from Trablus and Benghazi vilayets'. Cliopatria's Italian Africa row draws Libya from 1912; the two overlap in 1912 and the contest in the ledger marks the blend.

region.text: Tripoli and its surroundings, the seat of the restored Ottoman governor

ledger.note: 1835: the Ottomans reestablish direct control of Tripolitania. 'In 1835 the government of Sultan Mahmud II took advantage of local disturbances to reassert their direct authority'; the page's infobox dates 'Ottoman direct control re-established (1835)'. The month is the end of Ali II's reign on the Karamanli page.

region.text: Cyrenaica, the Gulf of Sidra and Fezzan, the sanjaks of Benghazi and Fezzan

ledger.note: 1835: the rest of the Karamanli province passes under the governor at Tripoli. The page lists five sanjaks in the 19th century (Tarablus al-Gharb, Khums, Jabal al-Garb, Fezzan and Benghazi/Cyrenaica); the land outside Tripolitania proper is read from the 1840 shape.

1865: the province is reclassified from an eyalet to a vilayet. The page: 'reclassified from an eyalet to a vilayet after an administrative reform in 1865' and 'by 1867 it had been reformed into the Tripolitania Vilayet'. The land is unchanged.

region.text: the coastal towns captured between 3 and 21 October 1911: Tripoli, Homs (Khums), Bengasi, Derna and Tobruk

ledger.note: 3 October 1911: Italy bombards Tripoli. The war was declared on 29 September 1911; operations began with the bombardment of Tripoli on 3 October and the city was taken by 1,500 sailors; Tripoli, Tobruk, Derna, Bengasi and Homs were captured between 3 and 21 October (the page is inconsistent on Tobruk: 4 December).

region.text: the coastal towns held by Italy

ledger.note: 18 October 1912: the Treaty of Ouchy ends the war. 'The Ottomans would withdraw all military personnel from Trablus and Benghazi vilayets'; the vilayets get a special status with a naib and a Caliph's kadi. The page says the treaty 'failed to bring peace to Libya': the Senussi refused to surrender.

region.text: Tripolitania, Fezzan and Cyrenaica, ceded to Italy by the treaty

ledger.note: 18 October 1912: the Ottomans give up Libya. The infobox gives Italy 'coastal areas of Tripolitania, Cyrenaica, and the Dodecanese Islands', the Ottoman Tripolitania page says the Turks 'ceded the provinces of Tripolitania, Fezzan, and Cyrenaica to Italy'; a decree of 5 November 1911 had already 'declared Italian sovereignty over Libya'. The Fezzan interior stayed beyond Italian control for years (the Fezzan page: 'precarious until at least 1923').

region.text: the province in its last year

ledger.note: October 1912: Ottoman Tripolitania ends. The Italo-Turkish War page: the coastal areas 'became Italian Tripolitania and Cyrenaica, which later merged into Italian Libya'; after the treaty the Senussi 'controlled most of Libya' and by 1 August 1915 Italy held only coastal enclaves. The Ottoman Tripolitania page puts Ottoman rule 'from 1551 to 1912'.

wars.name: Italo-Turkish War

zones.text: the coastal towns of Tripolitania and Cyrenaica captured in October 1911

wars.outcome: Italian victory: 'Italian victory' in the infobox, Italy gains the coastal areas of Tripolitania and Cyrenaica and the Dodecanese; the Treaty of Ouchy of 18 October 1912 has the Ottomans withdraw their troops and leaves a naib and a Caliph's kadi.
wars.note: 29 September 1911 - 18 October 1912. Local Libyans and the Senussi fought with the Ottoman officers (Enver, Mustafa Kemal, Fethi) and refused to surrender after the treaty; Mustafa Kemal won at Tobruk on 22 December 1911.

certainty.note: No frontier of the province is on any page: the Saharan, Fezzan and Cyrenaican limits are tribal and the Tunisian frontier is unfixed.

The Tunisian frontier is sharp: 'a border on the coast between Tunisia and Tripolitania in 1886', extended 'down to the vicinity of Ghadames in 1892', delimited by the treaty of 19 May 1910 and demarcated with pillars in 1910-11 (Libya-Tunisia page). Every other frontier stays soft.

sources.title: Ottoman Tripolitania
sources.note: Identity, capital, 1835, eyalet to vilayet 1865, five sanjaks, Cyrenaica 1863/1871/1888, Italian cession. Silent on the Saharan boundary agreements and on area.

sources.title: Italo-Turkish War
sources.note: 29 September 1911 - 18 October 1912, coastal captures, 5 November 1911 decree, Treaty of Ouchy.

sources.title: Fezzan
sources.note: Fezzan occupied by Italy from 1911, precarious until 1923; used for the 1912 cession note.

sources.title: Libya-Tunisia border
sources.note: 1886 coast border, 1892 extension to Ghadames, treaty of 19 May 1910, pillars 1910-11.

sources.title: Algeria-Libya border
sources.note: Thin: silent on the Ottoman-era frontier of Ghat and Ghadames; 1919 Franco-Italian treaty is after this state.

notes: Ottoman Tripolitania (af-02-f). (1) Span: Cliopatria 1840-1911; the page gives direct Ottoman control from 1835 and the treaty of 18 October 1912, so the dossier runs 1835-1912 with two new keyframes (1835-1839, 1912). The Karamanli dossier ends in May 1835 and its 1836 Cliopatria shape is marked wrong; Cliopatria's Ottoman Empire row holds 87 Tripolitanian cells in 1836-1839 that the ottoman-empire dossier (me-10) should drop. (2) Cliopatria's 1840-1884 shapes carry a stray 12.5 k km2 patch in Somaliland (47 cells at 10 N, 44-45 E), a few cells on the Tunisian edge and two on the Chad and Niger edge; both 1840 and 1859 are marked adjust (cut to Libya). The patch is probably the Egyptian-Ottoman Red Sea coast of 1870-1884 (Zeila, Berbera) mislabelled; the khedivate-of-egypt dossier (me-10) should check. (3) Kufra, the Tibesti and Borku hinterland and the Anglo-French Sahara declarations (1890, 1898-99, 1902) are on no page opened; the Ottoman page and the Algeria-Libya page are silent. The 1895 and 1905 shape changes (a few cells on the Saharan edge) are left unverified. (4) Cyrenaica's administration (independent sanjak 1863, under Tripoli 1871, directly under Istanbul 1888) changes no border and is recorded only in notes. The Senussi order (Jaghbub, Kufra) is a rival authority, not a state in Cliopatria; no dossier. (5) Neighbours in the seed: the Beylik of Tunis (1840-1884), Muhammad Ali dynasty and Khedivate of Egypt (to 1884: the shape's east edge is the 25 E Egyptian frontier, on no page opened), British Africa and French Africa (1885-1911: Sudan, Chad and Niger frontiers, on no page opened); only the Tunisian frontier is dated (1886, 1892, 1910) and no gain or loss is recorded with these neighbours because no page gives one. (6) The page says Italy gains 'coastal areas' while another sentence has the Turks cede 'Tripolitania, Fezzan, and Cyrenaica'; the loss is therefore confidence 2. The cessation date month (October 1912) follows the Italo-Turkish War page. Italian Africa's 1912 shape (2,946 Libyan cells) is the same land as this row's 1911 shape.
